chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhur, from his father, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the marriage of Shighaar, and it is Al-Mumanah, and it is that a man says to another man, 'Marry your daughter to me so that I may marry my daughter to you,' on the condition that there is no dower between them.
ai.seo_question: What is Shighaar marriage and why did the Prophet forbid it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi defines 'Shighaar' as a pre-Islamic practice where two men exchange daughters in marriage without paying dowry (mahr) to either bride, a custom the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) explicitly forbade. In Shia jurisprudence, this prohibition underscores that mahr is an essential, distinct right of the wife, not merely a reciprocal barter, thereby preserving the dignity and financial security of women within the marital contract.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhour, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said;

‘Rasool-Allahsaww forbade from the Shighaar marriage, and it is the Mumanahat, and it is that the man is saying to the man, ‘Marry your daughter to me and I shall marry my daughter to you upon a stipulation that there would be no dower between the both of them’’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Jumhur from his father in a marfu’ manner who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, prohibited marriage in the manner of Shighar which is giving away and it is done by one man’s saying to the other man, ‘Give your daughter in marriage to me so that I give my daughter in marriage to you and that there will be no mahr (dower) for anyone of them.’”
